prompts.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create one 3:2 landscape illustration for the existing Chinese history children's game. Reference images are ONLY the painterly children's-book style and fixed identities: exactly three modern Chinese children, yellow-jacket spiky black-haired boy without glasses, red/orange-jacket high-ponytail girl with flower clip, green-jacket straight-fringe boy with clear round glasses; familiar friendly adult guide in teal if useful. Keep children easily distinguishable, full faces and hands visible, finely painted warm gouache textures, no cheap flat clipart. No writing, captions, speech bubbles, watermarks or invented inscriptions. All objects are teaching story props; no claim that the illustration is a historical photograph. The friends safely stand on a grassy riverbank observing a low elegant Chinese stone bridge inspired by Zhaozhou Bridge. Clear side view of the bridge with ONE broad central arch and exactly FOUR smaller open shoulder arches, two per side. The river is calm and visible through the main arch; the bridge deck gently slopes, a small cart with a villager crosses above. The yellow boy points to the central large opening, the girl points to a small side arch, the green boy compares the safe path across the top with the water below. Avoid making a high steep rainbow bridge or several equal large arches. The bridge occupies the upper central and right half, friends lower left; clear separation of deck, openings, water. Rich natural trees and sunlight, intriguing discovery, no flooding disaster.

A peaceful spring evening in a Chinese garden viewed from a sheltered wooden window. The three friends and guide listen quietly to fine rain, with gently curious expressions and restrained gestures; one child cups an ear. Outside, clear thin rain streaks wet the leaves and pink blossoms near the window; dark blue river in distance has a small warm boat lantern, a soft transition toward a pale pre-dawn horizon. Keep night sky, small boat light, wet leaves and flowers recognizable as distinct observations. This is an imaginative interpretation of a poem, no identifiable portrait of Du Fu, no modern electric city skyline, no frightening storm. Cozy inside amber light contrasts with tranquil teal-blue night, poetic painterly atmosphere. Do not grow gigantic plants or show supernatural sentient rain.

At a modern museum textile demonstration table, an older woman demonstrator with simple hair and clothes gently teaches the three friends how cotton becomes yarn and cloth, evoking Huang Daopo's transmission of craft without claiming to be her portrait. On the LEFT foreground a wooden bowl holds fluffy raw white cotton with a few dark seeds; in the MIDDLE a clear ball and spool of creamy yarn; on the RIGHT a small simple wooden hand-weaving frame shows a partly woven cream and indigo cloth with visible crossing threads. The objects are large and separated on the tabletop, not obscured by hands. Yellow boy studies cotton, girl follows the thread toward cloth, green boy in round glasses watches the woman show yarn. Fine wood, fiber and woven textures; gentle cooperative scene. Avoid a modern industrial powered machine, invented precise mechanics, symbols or text.

In the MIDDLE, a small group of robed monks and sailors cooperate carrying wrapped BOOK bundles aboard a wooden sea-going sailing vessel, the book bundles clearly visible and protected from water. On the RIGHT the calm sea and a departing ship suggest the journey east. One elderly monk in simple robes is part of the group, not a verified portrait, no supernatural light or power. Monks and sailors help each other; no one floats on water, no child operates the ship. Two distinct observation points: bundled books at gangway and people helping one another aboard. No modern flags, charts with invented text, or Japanese tourist buildings. Warm morning light, rich historic harbor atmosphere as fictional teaching illustration.
